evidence_items.summary: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. However, current agents still struggle to finish such tasks, where success requires following long-horizon professional workflows, understanding heterogeneous file contexts, and producing usable deliverables under fine-grained requirements. A key bottleneck is the lack of scalable post-training data that reflects real work intent, authentic file environments, and deliverable-level evaluation. To close this gap, we introduce Agent-R^2, a real-source data synthesis framework that scales training data for realistic productivity work. Instead of relying on manually specified workflows or LLM-generated files, Agent-R^2 grounds synthesis throughout the pipeline in real occupational seeds, corpus-derived workflow evidence, and authentic web-sourced files. From 10k web-corpus candidates, Agent-R^2 distills 4k task instances that pair real multi-format attachments with fine-grained, deliverable-level rubrics. On this data, we train Agent-R^2-4B via supervised fine-tuning and rubric-based reinforcement learning, improving both end-to-end productivity performance and file-grounded reasoning. Trained on only 4k instances, Agent-R^2-4B surpasses Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 on both GDPval (51.0% vs. 48.0%) and OfficeQA (14.8% vs. 13.8%). Further analysis shows that Agent-R^2 mitigates shortcut behavior, where agents produce superficially plausible deliverables before sufficiently grounding, constructing, or verifying them, while promoting sustained exploration.
evidence_items.title: Agent-R^2: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis

evidence_items.summary:
PURPOSE
To map the development of research on large language models (LLMs) in radiology from November 2022 to July 2026, focusing on publication trends, collaboration patterns, citation distribution, and thematic shifts among Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE)-indexed original research articles.


METHODS
A bibliometric analysis was conducted using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Terms related to LLMs and radiology were combined at the topic (title, abstract, and keyword) level, and records retrieved by a complementary title-restricted strategy were screened jointly so that the analytic corpus reflected the union of both strategies. Only original research articles indexed in the SCIE were included. Records were screened independently by three reviewers (Fleiss' κ: 0.67). Publication trends, leading countries, institutions, authors, and journals; international collaboration networks; keyword co-occurrence patterns; citation distributions; and period-stratified thematic shifts were analyzed. Citation concentration was assessed with year-stratified sensitivity analyses, and a post hoc vision-language and foundation model sensitivity search quantified recent literature not captured by the primary strategy.


RESULTS
A total of 850 SCIE-indexed articles were included. Annual output increased from 1 article in 2022 to 380 in 2025 (2026 partial). The dataset accumulated 10,767 citations (mean 12.67 per article; Hirsch index 48), but impact was concentrated: The 10% most cited articles accounted for 63.8% of all citations, and 28.5% of articles were uncited (8.0% excluding the partial 2026 window). The United States was the most productive country and the most connected hub of international collaboration by total link strength and betweenness centrality, followed by China, Germany, and Türkiye. Publications concentrated in a small number of high-impact journals, led by Radiology. Keyword and period-stratified analyses showed a shift from early ChatGPT-centered feasibility studies toward general LLM and modality-specific evaluation, with keyword-level signals of an emerging multimodal direction.


CONCLUSION
Research on LLMs in the SCIE-indexed radiology literature has expanded rapidly since 2022. Keyword patterns suggest a gradual shift from exploratory, text-only applications toward clinically oriented evaluation, with early keyword-level signals of a multimodal direction, although methodological heterogeneity and the absence of standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks remain the main barriers to clinical adoption.


CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
By quantifying where, by whom, and on which themes LLM research in radiology is produced, this analysis helps radiologists, researchers, and funders identify under-studied modalities and applications, locate established collaboration networks, and direct future work toward the standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks the field currently lacks.
evidence_items.title: Large language models in radiology: a bibliometric analysis of growth, collaboration, and thematic shifts (November 2022-July 2026).

evidence_items.summary: Pretrained chemical language models are selected, embedded with, and fine tuned on the basis of what their documentation says they are. We report that the released model card for MoLFormer, one of the most widely used chemical foundation models, states that isomeric information was removed from its training data, and that this statement is contradicted by artifacts distributed in the model's own repository. The shipped token frequency table records the tetrahedral stereocentre token [C@H] occurring 669,642,207 times, making it the twelfth most frequent token in a corpus of 47.2 billion tokens, ahead of fluorine, and stereochemical tokens account for 3.17% of all token occurrences. The described stripping is real but occurs at a different pipeline stage: isomeric = False is hardcoded into the fine tuning scripts and applied to downstream benchmark data, not to pretraining. We find a related divergence in SMI-TED, whose released vocabulary contains 2,393 tokens rather than the 2,988 reported, and whose shipped frequency table is identical to MoLFormer's, byte for byte, across all 2,357 shared tokens, despite the paper describing a different corpus. We release the extracted frequency table and an audit tool, and recommend that chemical model cards state stereochemistry handling separately for pretraining, fine tuning, and inference.
evidence_items.title: Model cards are not primary artifacts: stereochemistry in the MoLFormer and SMI-TED chemical foundation models

evidence_items.summary: Document editing is among the most common knowledge-work tasks, yet existing benchmarks for evaluating autonomous agents on Word document editing provide fully specified attribute-modification instructions. They do not evaluate agents' ability to infer the appropriate attributes from document context, a capability essential in real-world editing where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute. We introduce WordInferBench, a benchmark comprising 280 base document-editing instances, each paired with three instruction conditions: descriptive (the instruction explicitly lists every attribute change), referential (the instruction points to another object as an exemplar), and inferential (the agent must examine document context to infer what attributes to apply). To evaluate contextual attribute inference, each base instance is constructed so that the target formatting is recoverable from an in-document exemplar. The instances are derived from real Word documents collected from Common Crawl and cover 13 object types and 81 attributes. We evaluate six recent coding-agent systems and find that the best-performing evaluated system, Claude Code with Opus 4.6, achieves a 62.9% task-level pass rate on descriptive variants but only 40.7% on inferential variants, indicating that current systems complete tasks less reliably when the required formatting changes must be determined from document context.
evidence_items.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?

evidence_items.summary: Tool-using language models are increasingly deployed in conversational settings, yet most large-scale tool-use benchmarks focus on isolated requests. We introduce ToolTurns, a benchmark of 2,620 problems spanning 1,827 tools and 11,004 API endpoints across 47 categories. Each dialogue begins with an intentionally underspecified request and continues through two context-dependent follow-ups, testing clarification, tool use, and retention of conversational context. We also introduce an open-source user simulator that reveals withheld context through dialogue and generates follow-up requests, with a checker--fixer pipeline for improving its turns. Across nine language models, the best agent resolves 69.6% of individual requests but completes only 39.8% of full dialogues. Under this evaluation protocol, every evaluated model receives lower success scores on follow-up requests than on the initial request, and dialogue-quality rubric scores and task success can rank models very differently. Paired turn-level evaluation shows that the checker--fixer reduces detected dialogue defects, and blind human evaluation favors the revised turns. ToolTurns provides a testbed for evaluating whether agents sustain task success across multi-turn dialogue with tools.
evidence_items.title: ToolTurns: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Dialogue

evidence_items.summary: Outline This is the Southern Ocean Anomaly Timeseries of Yamazaki et al. "Southern Ocean Ice Gauge" (Geophysical Research Letters, in review): monthly temperature and salinity anomalies of the upper 2000 m of the Southern Ocean for 2003–2025. The reconstruction method is Data Interpolating Empirical Orthogonal Functions (DINEOF; Beckers & Rixen, 2003). CTD data sourced from Argo floats and instrumented marine mammals (MEOP-CTD). Ship data were not included, to avoid their sampling bias toward summer and repeated sections, and served for independent validation. The anomalies are relative to the Southern Ocean Monthly Climatology (SOMC; Yamazaki et al., 2025; version v20240604, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13148501). Refer to the SOMC for the mean state: absolute temperature and salinity are the anomaly plus the SOMC averaged over its cells within each grid cell of this dataset. The dataset covers 75–40°S and 5–2000 m, monthly from January 2003 to December 2025 (2003–2004 serves as the spin-up years; the paper analyses 2005–2025). The bin-averaged observations used as its input are provided in " binned".
evidence_items.title: Southern Ocean Anomaly Timeseries

evidence_items.summary: This resource contains model descriptions for all models that participated in the GB Hydro-MIP Phase 1. These model descriptions follow the Scientific Model Description (SMD) questionnaires developed by the Environment Agency as part of a wider framework of model evaluation for operational flood hydrology. The questionnaires consisted of 82 questions which aimed to capture consistent information on model background, process representation, and capabilities as well as practical constraints such as data requirements, runtimes and code availability. Providing these detailed model descriptions consistently across all models supports investigation of the driving factors leading to differences in model behaviour and performance. While these model descriptions were completed for the GB Hydro-MIP, the information provided is not specific to this application and can support other model intercomparison projects (MIPs) in the future.    Model descriptions are given both as a summary report detailing answers for each model including model schematics where given and an excel file enabling direct comparison between responses for different model structures.
evidence_items.title: Model descriptions for models participating in the GB Hydro-MIP

evidence_items.summary:
Background
Forecasts of population-level cardiovascular risk factors can support surveillance and planning, but annual country-level health series are often short. With only 30 or 39 annual values per target, model flexibility can outpace the information available for training, making leakage control, repeated temporal evaluation, and comparison with simple baselines essential.


Objective
The aim of this study is to compare statistical, classical machine-learning, and neural forecasting models for age-standardized prevalence of hypertension (ASPH) and mean total cholesterol (MTC) in Chinese men and to test whether attention or substantially greater neural capacity provides consistent predictive benefit.


Methods
The authors analyzed 2 officially sourced annual series: ASPH for Chinese men aged 30 to 79 years (1990-2019; 30 observations) and MTC for Chinese men aged 18 years or older (1980-2018; 39 observations). No series was interpolated, extrapolated, imputed, smoothed, spliced, or synthetically extended. Leakage-controlled expanding-window evaluation began after 21 observations and assessed 1-, 2-, and 5-year horizons. Classical machine-learning and neural models used a fixed primary lookback of 3 (L=3), with nested lookback selection disabled; neural models used 10 fixed seeds. Performance was assessed with root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error, mean absolute scaled error, root mean squared scaled error, symmetric mean absolute percentage error, directional accuracy, mean error, median error, diagnostic R², prespecified neural-ablation inference, empirical forecast-interval coverage, and computational-cost reporting.


Results
Statistical models had the lowest RMSE in all 6 target-horizon cells. Autoregressive integrated moving average won for ASPH at h=1 (RMSE 0.000178), h=2 (RMSE 0.000578), and h=5 (RMSE 0.004324), and for MTC at h=1 (RMSE 0.000400) and h=2 (RMSE 0.001479); error-trend-seasonal state space won for MTC at h=5 (0.006991). Classical machine-learning and primary neural models won no cells. Removing attention reduced RMSE in 5 of 6 ablation cells, while the compact architecture had lower RMSE than Original23K in 5 of 6 cells; formal differences were detected for both contrasts at ASPH h=1 and h=2, whereas ASPH h=5 (n=5) was descriptive only. Predictive intervals often undercovered. The benchmark completed all 7242 planned output-producing fits.


Conclusions
Simple statistical forecasting remained highly competitive in these short, retrospectively estimated annual series. Greater complexity did not ensure better point prediction, and neither attention nor larger capacity conferred a consistent advantage. Point accuracy did not ensure well-calibrated predictive uncertainty; findings were conditional on the 2 targets, target-specific horizons, and small evaluation samples.
evidence_items.title: Horizon-Aware Forecasting of Hypertension Prevalence and Mean Total Cholesterol in Chinese Men: Retrospective Leakage-Controlled Benchmark Study Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, and Neural Models.

evidence_items.summary: Requests for Information (RFIs) can delay and complicate large construction projects, yet their downstream effects on design revisions, field rework, and schedule are rarely traced. This paper proposes an RFI-to-field traceability framework for airport Project Management/Construction Management (PMCM) teams. The framework links each RFI to the resulting drawing revisions, field change orders (FCOs), Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), rework, and critical-path delay across four project systems (Procore, Oracle Unifier, Primavera P6, and Bluebeam), and adds a leakage-aware classifier that assigns each RFI to a low, medium, or high impact class using only information available at submission. Because the logs of the motivating airport case are confidential, the framework is evaluated on a synthetic benchmark of 2,400 RFIs over 48 months with known ground-truth links; the results therefore validate the pipeline and are not empirical findings about real projects. The tiered linkage recovered 89%–99% of true links at each stage, with precision of 57%–96% (lowest for NCR and schedule links), and linkage-derived impact labels agreed with ground truth (Cohen's κ = 0.88). With a time-ordered split, the best early-warning model (random forest) reached a macro-F1 of 0.39 (95% CI 0.36–0.43) and ROC-AUC of 0.62 against a macro-F1 of 0.26 for a majority-class baseline, i.e., weak discrimination under the assumed noise. No cost or schedule saving is claimed; replication on anonymized real logs with a manual link audit is required.
evidence_items.title: RFI-to-Field Impact Analytics for Mega-Terminal Structural Packages: A Traceability Model Linking RFIs, Revisions, and Schedule Impacts

evidence_items.summary: High-dimensional portfolio optimization is a challenging computational problem due to its large search space, nonlinear objective structure, and practical constraints on asset allocation. To improve the computational tractability of Sharpe ratio-based portfolio optimization, this paper reformulates the original constrained model as an unconstrained single-objective problem by embedding equality and inequality constraints into the objective function through penalty terms. This reformulation simplifies constraint handling while retaining the financial interpretation of risk-return optimization. To solve the transformed problem, a quantum-inspired variant of Differential Evolution, termed Quantum-Inspired Differential Evolution with Elite Perturbation (QEPDE), is proposed. QEPDE extends the standard Differential Evolution framework through three complementary mechanisms. First, a good point set-chaos reverse learning strategy is introduced to generate a more diverse and well-distributed initial population. Second, a quantum-inspired population evolution strategy is designed to enhance global exploration and improve the flexibility of individual updates. Third, a dynamic elite pool with Cauchy-Gaussian hybrid perturbation is developed to preserve high-quality search information and reduce premature convergence. QEPDE is evaluated on the CEC 2020 and CEC 2022 benchmark suites, as well as four in-sample portfolio optimization instances involving 20, 40, 60, and 100 assets, and is compared with ADE, AVOA, DBO, DE, GWO, QHDBO, and WOA. On the CEC 2020 suite, QEPDE achieves the best results on 8 of the 10 functions at both 10 and 20 dimensions, with Friedman average ranks of 2.21 and 2.24, respectively. On the 20-dimensional CEC 2022 suite, QEPDE achieves the best results on 11 of the 12 functions and obtains the lowest Friedman average rank of 1.17. In the portfolio experiments, QEPDE achieves the highest mean penalized objective value on all four tested in-sample instances and the best or second-best mean Sharpe ratio across the four instances, while maintaining the full-investment constraint measure close to 1. These results indicate that QEPDE is competitive on the tested high-dimensional constrained optimization problems. All comparative performance statements in this abstract refer to the adopted equal-population-size and equal-iteration-count protocol rather than to an equal objective-function-evaluation budget.
evidence_items.title: Quantum-inspired differential evolution with Elite Perturbation for high-dimensional portfolio optimization

evidence_items.summary: The Two-Sided Assembly Line Balancing Problem (TSALBP) is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem. Although genetic algorithms (GAs) have been widely applied to TSALBP, many existing approaches suffer from premature convergence, limited scalability, and insufficient statistical validation. This paper proposes an Enhanced Genetic Algorithm (EGA) for TSALBP-1. The approach combines heuristic population initialization based on ranked positional weight and longest-path rules, adaptive crossover and mutation operators, earliest–latest station feasibility bounds, and a single-tier station assignment strategy. To improve workload distribution, a hybrid Tabu Search–Variable Neighborhood Search (TS/VNS) procedure is applied as a post-optimization stage. In addition, an AI-generated heuristic was developed, and its performance was compared with the proposed EGA and conventional algorithms. Performance was evaluated using solution-quality metrics and rigorous statistical analyses, including Friedman ranking, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and Dolan–Moré performance profiles. Experimental results show that the EGA achieved an average gap of only 0.34% from the lower bound and achieved the highest overall ranking among all competing heuristics. Five independent runs across all 42 benchmark configurations showed low run-to-run variability, supporting the robustness of the proposed EGA. Besides, the proposed approach consistently outperformed the AI-generated heuristic, especially for medium- and large-scale benchmark instances. Finally, the TS/VNS post-optimization phase improved workload balance significantly, reducing idle-time variance by up to 99.7% in large-scale instances. The results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive hybrid framework provides an effective and scalable solution for TSALBP while achieving superior solution quality, robustness, and workload distribution. While hybrid initialization, adaptive operators, and TS/VNS refinement are individually established techniques, the novelty of this work lies in their coordinated integration within a TSALBP-specific framework, their controlled component-wise evaluation, and the rigorous statistical validation of the overall framework. The main contributions of this work are the development of an enhanced adaptive genetic algorithm with heuristic-based population initialization and dynamic search operators, together with a hybrid TS/VNS post-optimization framework for smoothing workload without increasing the number of stations. In addition, the proposed approach is comprehensively validated through rigorous statistical analyses and benchmarked against both state-of-the-art algorithms and an AI-generated heuristic to assess the potential of large language models for generating heuristic solution procedures for TSALBP.
evidence_items.title: A robust hybrid metaheuristic framework for two-sided assembly line balancing with adaptive genetic search and post-optimization workload balancing

evidence_items.summary: For traditional IT development work, besides project design and development team, software testing engineers are also needed for code testing and quality management, which confronts much redundant and high-cost works. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, it is possible to find a new way for analyzing and evaluating source codes automatically and help to reduce redundant works and R&D costs caused by manual work. Based on the collection of source code data, this paper firstly describes the composition of structured programming corpus, and then analyzes code structure at the abstract syntax tree (AST) level in order to extract key features of those codes. Thirdly, a graph embedding-based vectorization algorithm is used to convert code and its abstract syntax trees into matrices and numerical representations. Fourthly, dimensionality reduction algorithms or optimization methods directly used are designed and applied for multidimensional process and principal feature extraction. Lastly, an adaptive hierarchical clustering method is used to achieve optimal partitioning of data samples. This paper elaborates basic principles, main components and implementation for constructing intelligent evaluation systems of source codes and the final experiment results verifies this intelligent evaluation system could not only learn significant differences between correct code and erroneous code, but also provide good clustering performance and surpass the typical unsupervised learning algorithms, such as K-means, DEC, DAEGC.
evidence_items.title: Research on intelligent evaluation system of program algorithms used in IT development process

evidence_items.summary:
The integration of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education shows promise but lacks empirical evidence of effectiveness. This study evaluated a customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4-based conversational agent designed explicitly for a pharmacology block in undergraduate medical education.
 
 
 
 A mixed-methods sequential explanatory design was employed in a four-week elective pharmacology block at the College of Medicine, Sulaiman Al-Rajhi University. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional survey of enrolled students (n = 58) who used the AI tool, with a comparative analysis of their academic performance against historical cohorts without access to AI (2022–2023: n = 33; 2023–2024: n = 37). Academic performance was measured through mid-block quizzes, end-of-block examinations, and total block score. Phase 2 comprised semi-structured interviews (n = 9), transcribed and analyzed thematically.
 
 
 
 The survey response rate was 89.6% (52/58), and 98.1% (51/52) reported using the tool. Among users, 74.5% engaged with the GPT tool daily. Students reported exceptionally high satisfaction: 92.2% found it more effective than traditional methods, 94.1% felt it made learning more engaging, and the likelihood of recommending it averaged 4.65 ± 0.73 (on a 5-point scale). Frequency of use was significantly associated with perceived improvement in learning (χ2 = 15.84, p < 0.05). Academic performance showed marginal, non-significant improvements: total scores increased by 2.5% (75.52 vs. 77.40, p > 0.05), with pass rates improving from 92.9% to 98.3% (p > 0.05). Qualitative analysis revealed six themes: learning support and academic enhancement; efficiency and accessibility; GPT's supplementary role in learning; perceived strengths and unique features; limitations and challenges; and suggestions for improvement.
 
 
 
 The disconnect between exceptional user engagement and minimal performance improvements challenges traditional evaluation paradigms. While conversational AI may not directly enhance examination scores, students' accounts suggest it may support metacognitive development, reduce cognitive load, and foster critical-thinking skills essential for modern medical practice, thereby necessitating multidimensional assessment frameworks.
evidence_items.title: Beyond grades to learning enhancement: development, implementation and evaluation of a conversational AI agent in medical education

evidence_items.summary: Study DesignDiagnostic accuracy study.ObjectiveTo determine whether a general-purpose multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini 3 Pro, grades lumbar neuroforaminal stenosis on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in agreement with expert radiologists, particularly for severe stenosis, and whether a vertebral-level localizer overlay helps.MethodsOne hundred lumbar MRIs from the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) 2024 Lumbar Spine Degenerative Classification Dataset, graded by expert radiologists, provided 1,000 foramina (five levels, both sides) labeled normal/mild, moderate, or severe. Sagittal and axial T2-weighted series were converted into short scrolling videos and submitted to the model with a structured grading prompt; no task-specific training was performed. The primary outcome was agreement with expert grades (linearly weighted Cohen's kappa, κw); secondary outcomes were accuracy, severe-stenosis sensitivity, direction of errors, and the localizer effect.ResultsAgreement with expert grading was poor (κw 0.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.14-0.26). Accuracy was 70.6% (95% CI 67.7-73.4) but reflected the 70.4% of foramina that were normal/mild. The model identified 17.9% of severe foramina (95% CI 8.9-30.4) and called 58.9% normal/mild. Errors were systematically toward undergrading (p < 0.001). The localizer did not improve accuracy (70.0% vs 70.6%, p = 0.590) and reduced severe sensitivity (3.6% vs 17.9%, p = 0.043).ConclusionsWithout task-specific training, a general-purpose AI model reached moderate accuracy only because most foramina were normal or mild; it missed most severe stenosis and systematically undergraded. In its current form this approach is unsuitable for screening, triage, operative decision-making, or independent report generation.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating Multimodal Vision Frontier Models for Grading Neuroforaminal Stenosis on Lumbar Spine MRIs.

evidence_items.summary:
Background
Imaging-based AI may help predict pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy for esophageal cancer. However, an encouraging average diagnostic performance does not establish reliable performance across clinical settings or justify treatment decisions without further validation.


Objective
We aimed to assess the predictive performance of imaging-based AI across neoadjuvant strategies, distinguish internal from external validation, and examine limitations affecting interpretation.


Methods
PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through August 7, 2026. Eligible English-language studies evaluated imaging-based AI against pathological assessment of pCR. PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool plus Artificial Intelligence) assessed study quality and risk of bias; GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) assessed certainty for sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Bivariate random-effects models synthesized validation groups separately. CIs described uncertainty in average performance, whereas 95% prediction intervals (PIs) described true performance in a similar new study.


Results
Thirty-three studies contributed 27 internal-validation datasets with 1891 patients and 16 external-validation datasets with 777 patients. Ten publications contributed to both groups. The sum was 2668 validation observations; the unique patient count across datasets and publications could not be verified. Internal sensitivity was 0.77 (95% CI 0.72-0.81; PI 0.57-0.89), specificity 0.82 (95% CI 0.78-0.86; PI 0.60-0.93); DOR, 15.49 (95% CI 11.16-21.50); and area under the curve (AUC), 0.86 (95% CI 0.83-0.89). External sensitivity was 0.73 (95% CI 0.61-0.81; PI 0.34-0.93), specificity 0.83 (95% CI 0.73-0.90; PI 0.36-0.98), DOR 12.93 (95% CI 7.25-23.07), and AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.89). DOR PIs were 5.40-44.44 and 2.40-69.62, respectively. Thirty-two studies were conducted in China, and 12 had high validation risk of bias. All GRADE-assessed outcomes had very low certainty. Selecting the first eligible imaging model reported in each article instead of the highest-AUC model showed modest decreases in average performance across 16 internal and 10 external datasets; incomplete alternative-model reporting limited interpretation. Single study algorithm estimates were reported descriptively, without ranking algorithms or interpreting their CIs as evidence of between study consistency or generalizability.


Conclusions
By combining multiple neoadjuvant strategies and separating validation stages, this review extends earlier neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT)-focused syntheses and identifies priorities for further model evaluation. Imaging-based AI may support response assessment, but wide PIs, risk of bias, and very low evidence certainty preclude routine clinical adoption without prospective, geographically diverse validation. Future studies should evaluate prespecified models in independent populations, report clinically relevant decision thresholds, and assess calibration and patient outcomes. Until such evidence is available, these models should be considered investigational adjuncts to response assessment and should not independently guide organ preservation or omission of surgery after neoadjuvant treatment.
evidence_items.title: Imaging-Based AI for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Esophageal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Therapy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence_items.summary: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, primarily caused by blockages in coronary arteries due to plaques or fatty deposits. Early identification and precise diagnosis are crucial for timely treatment, reducing disease severity, improving patient quality of life, and preventing complications. Objective: To develop an advanced, interpretable, and accurate CVD detection framework that addresses limitations in conventional methods related to feature representation and capturing complex relationships within the data. The model initiates with data cleaning to eliminate errors and inconsistencies, followed by Dynamic Gaussian Piecewise Normalization (DGPN) to handle heterogeneous and complex datasets, thereby improving feature representation. Multiobjective Weighted Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBM) extract salient features, with weights optimized via a Revised Fitness-Oriented Bobcat Optimization Algorithm (RFO-BOA) employing multi-objective functions. An Adaptive Residual Capsule Network enhanced with Coordinate Attention (ARCCA) is employed to identify complex spatial and hierarchical patterns, increasing detection accuracy. The parameters of ARCCA are finely tuned through RFO-BOA to further elevate performance. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark cardiovascular datasets demonstrate the robustness and efficacy of the proposed model. The RFO-BOA–ARCCA approach achieved significant accuracy improvements of approximately 15.94%, 2.56%, 8.12%, and 3.89% over traditional models, including ANN, LSTM, SVM, and CapsNet, respectively. The integrated framework combining advanced data preprocessing, multi-objective feature extraction, and an optimized capsule network effectively facilitates early and accurate CVD detection. This framework holds promise for real-time clinical applications, enabling improved patient outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Time adaptive clinical data driven cardiovascular disease detection using multi-objective features-based residual CapsNet with coordinate attention

evidence_items.summary: Reproducibility remains a persistent challenge in transportation research, particularly in mixed-traffic studies involving connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). Driving simulators support controlled investigation of human–CAV interactions, but their experimental setups are often difficult to reproduce. Scenario geometry, traffic actors, controller logic, data logging, and pretesting procedures are frequently implemented through manual, bespoke, or poorly documented workflows. These limitations make experiment iteration time-consuming and error-prone, and they limit systematic assessment of whether a scenario is technically feasible under real-time human-in-the-loop operation. This paper proposes a reproducible design-to-implementation framework for mixed CAV driving-simulator experiments. The framework treats reproducibility as part of experiment design by linking parameterised experiment specification, scripted scenario generation, controller assignment, structured logging, pretesting, and benchmark-based feasibility checking. The framework is integrated and demonstrated within SimCCAD, a simulation platform for Conventional, Connected, and Automated Driving, through a scenario designed to investigate driver interactions with CAVs. The implementation shows how road geometry, traffic actors, controller logic, world files, and benchmarking outputs can be generated within an auditable project structure. The framework enables candidate scenario configurations to be generated, executed, and evaluated systematically under varying surrounding-CAV settings. This creates a reproducible basis for identifying feasible experiment configurations before participant deployment. The resulting workflow connects experiment design, executable simulator implementation, and benchmark-based feasibility evaluation within SimCCAD/Webots. Although the implementation is platform-specific, its underlying principles may also support mixed CAV studies on other platforms that provide equivalent mechanisms for parameterised design, scripted execution, documented refinement, and feasibility evaluation.
evidence_items.title: A framework for reproducible design, implementation, and evaluation of driving-simulator experiments in SimCCAD for mixed traffic research

evidence_items.summary: This article examines methodological and practical approaches to evaluating the fiscal effectiveness of tax incentives and optimizing tax expenditures. Tax expenditures are defined relative to a benchmark tax system, while the reported value of benefits used is distinguished from actual revenue forgone. Effectiveness is assessed through additional investment, employment, tax receipts and distributional outcomes rather than beneficiary take-up alone. The analysis draws on Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts report for 2025 and guidance issued by international institutions. Because publicly available aggregate statistics do not identify the causal effects of individual incentives, four explicitly hypothetical policy scenarios are compared. The article develops a sequential decision framework combining a comprehensive tax expenditure register, measurable targets, periodic evaluation, sunset provisions and comparisons with direct budget spending. The proposed approach emphasizes targeted redesign, transparent fiscal accounting and evidence-based prioritization instead of indiscriminate withdrawal of tax preferences. It also specifies the administrative data and quasi-experimental research designs needed for future impact evaluation.
evidence_items.title: Soliq imtiyozlarining fiskal samaradorligini baholash va soliq xarajatlarini optimallashtirish yo'nalishlari

evidence_items.summary: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for equipment reliability management and maintenance decision-making. However, in the presence of multiple fault modes and varying operating conditions, existing methods often struggle to achieve both reliable fault-mode identification and accurate, robust RUL prediction. Therefore, this paper proposes a fault-mode-aware RUL prediction framework based on differentiated multi-scale similarity matching with adaptive focal-scale activation. First, an autoencoder is employed to construct a degradation-sensitive and robust health index from healthy operating data. Subsequently, Temporal and Contextual Contrasting is used for unsupervised fault mode identification, ensuring that only same-mode degradation trajectories are retained as references. Finally, a differentiated multi-scale matching mechanism is developed using mean-residual comparison, dynamic time warping, and spherically weighted dynamic time warping at the short-term, full-life-cycle, and focal scales, respectively. Additionally, a sliding-threshold strategy is employed to facilitate focal-scale matching and accurately capture critical degradation stages. The experimental results indicate that the proposed method is superior to six advanced benchmark methods on the C-MAPSS dataset. Specifically, compared with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Encoder-Decoder, the proposed method reduces the root-mean-square error by 30.1%, 26.4%, 41.9%, and 20.3% across the four C-MAPSS subsets, with corresponding Score reductions of 46.7%, 50.5%, 54.6%, and 30.3%. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits high prediction accuracy, strong robustness, and excellent generalizability, demonstrating its potential for predictive maintenance of complex industrial equipment.
evidence_items.title: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Equipment With Multi-Failure-Mode Degradation Based on Multi-Scale Similarity Matching

evidence_items.summary: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are increasingly promoted for flood mitigation, yet how to allocate limited resources while balancing aggregate effectiveness and social equity remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether directing greater mitigation benefits toward socially vulnerable communities necessarily requires substantial losses in overall flood-susceptibility reduction. We develop an equity-aware multi-objective optimization framework for allocating tree planting and wetland restoration across census block groups under fixed budget, suitability, and intervention-capacity constraints. The framework explicitly represents the trade-off between aggregate flood-susceptibility reduction and vulnerability-weighted mitigation benefit, while high-priority locations are identified using a composite flood risk metric integrating flood susceptibility, population exposure, and social vulnerability. We apply the framework to Dorchester and Somerset Counties, Maryland, and evaluate exact optimization alongside greedy, random, and reinforcement-learning benchmarks. Under a USD 20 million budget, moderate vulnerability weighting produced substantial gains in vulnerability-weighted mitigation benefit with little loss in aggregate performance. In Dorchester, aggregate susceptibility reduction changed from 33.47% under the pure-efficiency solution to 33.21% under moderate vulnerability weighting, while vulnerability-weighted reduction increased from 40.48% to 42.06%. In Somerset, aggregate reduction changed from 31.97% to 31.62%, while vulnerability-weighted reduction increased from 34.58% to 36.37%; population-weighted reduction also increased slightly from 34.91% to 35.38%. The same trade-off persisted when expenditure and intervention mix were held constant and across alternative budgets, census-block-group inclusion thresholds, intervention assumptions, and parameter settings. Greedy allocation closely reproduced the exact optimum, whereas reinforcement learning remained substantially suboptimal, indicating that classical optimization is better suited to the deterministic allocation problem considered here. Overall, the results show that meaningful improvements in the distribution of NBS mitigation benefits toward socially vulnerable communities can be achieved at only a modest cost in aggregate flood-susceptibility reduction. The framework provides a transparent approach for evaluating equity–efficiency trade-offs in spatial flood-mitigation planning.
evidence_items.title: Equity-aware multi-objective optimization of nature-based solutions for flood susceptibility reduction

evidence_items.summary: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study. This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography. Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed. In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).
evidence_items.title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study

evidence_items.summary:
The heterogeneity of the disease and failures in biological therapy contribute to the socioeconomic challenges derived from ulcerative colitis (UC). Therefore, it is essential to identify factors that can aid in making targeted decisions. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) play a significant role in the development of intestinal inflammation. However, their potential for diagnosing, monitoring, or predicting biological therapy response has not been extensively studied.
 
 
 
 We conducted in silico analyses based on the expression of all MMP-related transcripts retrieved from publicly available microarray and RNAseq datasets of UC patients. For completeness, we also evaluated the expression of MME as a potential biomarker in blood cells from a local cohort of UC patients (n = 34) using RT-qPCR, and we assessed its involvement in the proteolytic degradation of different biologic agents.
 
 
 
 We found that the colonic transcript levels of thirteen MMPs were dysregulated in UC patients and were highly associated with disease activity. Furthermore, the expression of these MMPs (especially MME) at the colon level is linked to difficult-to-treat patients. Additionally, the expression of MME in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) effectively discriminated patients who failed anti-TNF therapy.
 Finally, the analysis of the cleavage pattern of infliximab and vedolizumab after incubation with recombinant MME revealed no effects on the integrity of these advanced therapies.
 
 
 
 Our findings enhance our understanding of the relationship between MMPs and UC, provide candidate biomarkers for the most aggressive phenotypes of UC, and propose an easy-to-read factor for predicting the response to anti-TNF therapy by analysing PBMCs.
evidence_items.title: Exploring the relevance of the matrix metalloproteinase family in ulcerative colitis patients

evidence_items.summary:
OBJECTIVE
This study aimed to isolate and characterize a lytic phage targeting Vibrio parahaemolyticus and evaluate its endolysin for potential application as antimicrobial agents.


METHODS
A phage was isolated from seawater using V. parahaemolyticus ATCC 17802 as host. Morphological, physiological, and genomic analyses were performed, followed by cloning and expression of the endolysin gene. The lytic activity and stability of the recombinant endolysin were assessed under different conditions. Finally, antimicrobial efficacy of phage and endolysin in combination with citric acid were tested on shrimp paste.


RESULTS
The phage Vp16M exhibited a short latent period, high burst size, and broad stability across temperature and pH ranges, with no virulence or resistance genes detected. Its endolysin Lys16M showed strong lytic activity, stability, and the Lys16M-citric acid combination resulted in a 2.4-log reduction of bacterial counts.


CONCLUSION
Phage Vp16M and endolysin Lys16M demonstrate promising antimicrobial properties and safety profiles, supporting their potential as biocontrol agents against V. parahaemolyticus.
evidence_items.title: Characterization of a lytic phage Vp16M (genus Maculvirus) and its endolysin against Vibrio parahaemolyticus.

evidence_items.summary:
This study examines diverse stakeholder perceptions of the effectiveness of environmental education in universities across the United Arab Emirates (UAE), situated within the country's broader sustainability and higher education policy context, including UAE Vision 2071.
 
 
 
 Using Q methodology as an application of stakeholder theory, the research captures subjective viewpoints from academic, professional and community groups to identify distinct discourses that represent varied conceptions of program success.
 
 
 
 Five distinct discourses emerged: (1) pragmatic innovators, who emphasise measurable outcomes and technological integration; (2) community-focused traditionalists, who value local engagement and established pedagogical methods; (3) global sustainability advocates, who promote international perspectives and climate action; (4) technical competency builders, who prioritise professional skill development; and (5) holistic experience seekers, who highlight transformative personal learning. These discourses map different ways participants in this purposively selected P-set conceptualised environmental education effectiveness; they do not estimate the prevalence of these viewpoints in the wider UAE stakeholder population.
 
 
 
 The study focuses on a selection of UAE universities, which may limit transferability to other national and institutional contexts. Q methodology reveals the structure and range of perspectives but does not measure their prevalence in the wider stakeholder population. Its cross-sectional design captures views at a single point in time, despite evolving environmental challenges and policy agendas. The 40-statement Q-sample, though carefully constructed, represents only a subset of possible viewpoints. Future work should include longitudinal, outcome-linked and cross-cultural studies to test the stability, impact and broader applicability of the identified discourses.
 
 
 
 Universities can use the five discourses as a stakeholder-informed framework for curriculum design, strategic planning and quality assurance in environmental education. Administrators are encouraged to adopt portfolio assessment systems capturing multiple indicators (technical, global, community, experiential) and to institutionalise participatory governance mechanisms. Faculty can design flexible curricular blocks and diverse pedagogies – ranging from technology-enhanced learning and internships to community-based and experiential approaches – aligned with different discourses. Policymakers can support institutional diversity and sustained stakeholder engagement through funding schemes and incentives that recognise plural conceptions of effectiveness.
 
 
 
 By foregrounding diverse stakeholder perspectives, the study supports more inclusive, culturally responsive and socially just environmental education in the UAE. It highlights tensions between technocratic, employment-focused models and community-rooted, holistic and transformative priorities, surfacing issues of power and representation in educational decision-making. Integrating critical pedagogy, ecojustice and decolonial perspectives, the study argues for environmental programs that honour local knowledge, address socio-environmental inequities and cultivate empowered, critically conscious graduates. Such programs can enhance social cohesion and ethical stewardship while advancing the UAE's long-term sustainability vision.
 
 
 
 The study contributes to sustainability education literature by providing an empirically derived, multi-stakeholder map of how environmental education effectiveness is understood within the UAE higher-education context. Participants' post-sort accounts also show that these viewpoints are interpreted within a national policy environment in which sustainability leadership, workforce preparation and Emiratisation are salient considerations. The five-discourse typology is not presented as a validated benchmarking instrument; rather, it provides a theoretically grounded basis that could inform the future development and validation of evaluation or benchmarking tools.
evidence_items.title: Diverse voices, shared goals: stakeholder perspectives on environmental education effectiveness in UAE universities

evidence_items.summary: The Africa Union's (AU's) response to the military takeover in Africa involves condemning and suspending countries from the continental organisation due to undemocratic and unconstitutional political power changes. However, the persistent occurrence of coups in West Africa, alongside the entrenchment of authoritarian regimes, calls into question the effectiveness of strategies employed by African Union (AU). The study examined effectiveness of the intervention strategies by African Union in curtailing coups d'etat in West Africa (2014 – 2024). The contagious theory was adopted as a guide. Information/data for the study was generated from both primary and secondary sources. Personal Interviews were employed as instruments for primary data, while for secondary method, sources like research papers, policy papers, documents, journals, magazines, seminars, workshop papers and handbook were utilized. The study shows that the current intervention strategies employed by AU are insufficient to prevent democratic backsliding and mitigate the impact of military coups in West Africa. The study established that in spite of sanctions, these states are yet to handover to the deposed government or a transitional government and have remained under the military governments. Upon closer examination, the AU appears to have a mixed record, particularly in implementing its Unconstitutional Change of Government (UCG) policy especially in regards to coups. The study recommended that stability can be aided by addressing problems like unemployment, inequality, and poverty as they can lessen the chance of military involvement. Above all, there should be benign democratic governance. It is only people-oriented governments that can guarantee good life to the citizens when it upholds economic conditions and improve state capacity to manage its affairs effectively.
evidence_items.title: DEMOCRATIC REVERSALS AND MILITARY TAKEOVERS IN WEST AFRICA: AN EVALUATION OF AFRICAN UNION PEACE AND SECURITY INITIATIVES

evidence_items.summary: Version 1 of the "Time resolved bottleneck analysis", also available on https://forge.inrae.fr/sylvain.vicente/time-resolved-bottleneck-analysis. Time-resolved-bottleneck-analysis Description This code is a minimal reproducible example to apply the analyses developed in the preprint "Time-resolved bottlenecks reveal concurrent pathogen entry and growth during bacterial infection dynamics" (BioRXiv DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.21.689558 ). Given a population of neutral diversity, the analysis infers on the most probable scenario of bottleneck/founder event that shaped this diversity (among 5 models, described in reference). Each model compares an initial population ("inoculum") to a final population ("sample") and estimates whether it is plausible that the diversity in the final population could be generated from the initial population. Each model's fit is compared under a unified metric: the Hill Distance ("D"). The Hill Distance summarises the error between the model's best simulated diversity profiles versus real sample profiles. A low Hill Distance indicates that the model accurately reproduces diversity patterns seen in the samples. Additionally to the model's fit, a bottleneck strength term (denoted "theta") is calculated for each sample. This term estimates whether the bottleneck is stringent (low number of passing lineages) or permissive (high number of passing lineages). For some models, additional metrics like the growth rate parameter ("r") or the entry rate parameter ("mu") are also derived from theta, CFU and time. Usage The code is provided within a partially controlled environment (the R project "Time-resolved-bottleneck-analysis"). The R markdown notebook "Analysis toolset.Rmd" contains the code to apply the time-resolved bottleneck analysis on a dummy dataset and can be launched using RStudio. The dummy dataset is provided in the folder "Analysis output".
evidence_items.title: Time resolved bottleneck analysis

evidence_items.summary: This report and reproducibility package examine how a specified receiver determines which distinctions in a supplied nested quantum state become accessible in its measurement records. Two nonorthogonal states with unequal 70/30 population weights and opposite coherence have identical reduced states on every nonempty proper subset of their encoded registers. Measurements confined to those subsets cannot distinguish the candidates. Local equatorial measurements followed by comparison of their records reveal a joint parity contrast, whose accessibility depends on the receiver phase. For the worked two-register example, equal-prior single-trial discrimination succeeds with probability 95.83% under ideal retention and 79.33% with independent 80% retention at each receiver. These probabilities include incomplete records. Blind receiver settings and complete dephasing provide distinct zero-contrast controls. The report also establishes reconstruction from three real quantities within a known two-dimensional encoded subspace. A support-leakage counterexample demonstrates why this reconstruction does not extend to unrestricted states. All sixteen numerical check families pass, including 5,130 proper-subset comparisons. A verification run reproduces the archived scientific results exactly. The package includes the report, executable code, fixed configuration, numerical results, probability tables, figures, equation sources, report builder and checksums. This is an analytic and computational benchmark within declared quantum states and measurement models. It provides a bounded example of receiver-dependent information access and candidate-state identification; it does not constitute experimental validation or derive a physical mechanism of nesting.
evidence_items.title: Receiver Distinguishability of Nested States

evidence_items.summary: Acute respiratory tract infection (ARI) is the most common reason for consulting in primary care (PC) sites, such as general practices (GPs), urgent care centres, and paediatric care centres. Moreover, new and re-emerging pathogens are often first noticed in primary care. There are four important areas of focus in the management of ARI in primary care: 1. Accurate diagnosis and prediction of complications; 2. Making appropriate antibiotic and antiviral prescribing decisions; 3. Optimising patient care and treatment in an epidemic or pandemic situation; 4. Prevention, for example through vaccination. POS-ARI-PC is a multi-country, prospective Perpetual Observational Study (POS) among patients presenting in PC with symptoms of ARI. It aims to provide an estimate of the overall incidence of illness and individual diagnoses, as well as critically important benchmark descriptive data related to patient characteristics, complications, outcome, and risk factors per viral aetiology. These detailed data allow for the identification of variation in management and care within and between countries, suggesting improvements for care planning and informing clinical guidelines. In the longer term, the study will establish a research-ready infrastructure for enhanced observational studies and clinical trials related to treatment, diagnosis, and prevention of ARI in the primary care setting. Such a “plug-in” approach is especially beneficial during epidemics and pandemics because it makes it possible to set up new studies much quicker, without having to go through the full process of regulatory approvals for each individual research.
