evidence_items.summary: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.
evidence_items.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents

evidence_items.summary: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models and using 2.1M-3.8M training pairs from public datasets, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU) and rivals state-of-the-art affine-invariant depth estimators. Its non-zero-shot variants come within five points of Vision Banana on referring and reasoning segmentation but remain further behind on instance segmentation. All models largely retain the base model's image-editing abilities. With legend ensembling, we introduce a test-time scaling method for generator-based perception. It segments an image under several class-color legends and fuses the results by majority vote, correcting unstable color-class bindings and improving mIoU by up to 8.7 points on Cityscapes and 15.0 points on COCO-Object without retraining. We release the dataset construction and processing pipeline, the training and evaluation code, as well as the final, intermediate, and ablation checkpoints. Project website: https://openvisionbanana.github.io
evidence_items.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception

evidence_items.summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria; and realistic interactive evaluation, where models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes. Reasoning-intensive tasks further enable system one-two comparison. Beyond accuracy, SO-Arena assesses decision reliability through two complementary measures: decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition when no valid option is available. Evaluations across 21 models reveal that the benefits of scaling and additional reasoning vary substantially across domains. More importantly, strong overall performance does not necessarily imply reliable decision-making: the best-performing System One model ranks only seventh in reliability. Together, these findings highlight the need to characterize capability spectrum and decision reliability as complementary dimensions, providing a systematic view of the strengths and limitations of System One models.
evidence_items.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models

evidence_items.summary: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer poorly across tasks. We further propose instruction-faithful criteria and show that they better reflect the performance of agent-generated programs.
evidence_items.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
Comparison of components and processes among river catchment systems using interaction matrices prepared for different climate conditions using Fukushima case as a benchmark.

evidence_items.summary: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) is a patient-centered outcome in pediatric burn care, yet no burn-specific, validated German-language instrument is available for this population. This study evaluated the feasibility and measurement properties of the German PedsQL™ 4.0 Generic Core Scales (GCS) in pediatric outpatients after thermal injuries. In this retrospective observational study, the authorized German PedsQL™ 4.0 GCS was implemented in a pediatric burn clinic. Data from October 2022 to January 2026 were analyzed across 16 age-, respondent-, and recall-specific forms. Feasibility, internal consistency (model-based omega total), structural validity (ordinal confirmatory factor analysis of parent-proxy reports), floor and ceiling effects, known-groups validity, and responsiveness were assessed. Patients were the unit of analysis; analysis windows (0–30 and ≥ 31 days after the patient-specific index) were distinct from questionnaire recall versions. Of 1,194 questionnaire opportunities, 951 (79.6%) were completed; language barriers accounted for 42.0% of non-completions. Parent-proxy and child self-report index samples comprised 382 and 134 patients. The parent-proxy Total Score averaged 80.73, with Emotional functioning the lowest (73.61). Of 96 form-by-scale coefficients, 75 were estimated; Emotional functioning point estimates exceeded 0.70 in all forms, although precision was frequently limited, whereas the Total Score was estimable in seven forms (0.814–0.945), and Physical, Social, and Cognitive/School values below 0.70 occurred only in 8–12-year or adolescent forms. No model achieved adequate global fit (correlated four-factor model, n = 244: CFI = 0.865; RMSEA = 0.120). Ceiling effects reached 55.2% for Social and 42.0% for Cognitive/School functioning, without relevant floor effects. Known-groups differences were confined to parent-proxy Physical Summary (adjusted p = 0.030; δ = −0.238). In 122 paired patients, Total and Physical Summary Scores increased by 4.98 (95% CI 2.80–7.16) and 6.63 (3.45–9.82) points, with no consistent evidence of Social improvement. The German PedsQL™ 4.0 GCS was feasible for routine use and showed generally adequate internal consistency in several larger form-by-scale analyses. Group-level monitoring requires attention to form, domain, sample size, and structural-fit limitations. Structural validity was only partially supported and examined in parent-proxy reports alone; content validity and invariance were not evaluated. Ceiling effects require cautious interpretation.
evidence_items.title: Validity and reliability of the pediatric quality of life inventory™ 4.0 generic core scales to measure health-related quality of life in pediatric outpatients after thermal injuries

evidence_items.summary: The number of papers published in health promotion journals has grown substantially for two decades, and mainstream use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has accelerated that growth. Yet peer review remains fundamentally unchanged. Review still depends on volunteer time, and many journals prohibit reviewers from using AI to protect confidential, unpublished work. The result is an asymmetry: authors write faster with AI, while reviewers face mounting demand without the same tools. Funding agencies have begun responding; the NIH, for example, now caps annual application submissions per principal investigator. Journals cannot impose comparable limits because submissions are scattered across thousands of independent outlets, and requiring authors to complete reviews in proportion to their publications would be nearly impossible to enforce. We propose a solution that concentrates limited reviewer capacity on the most complex and consequential research. Cross-sectional and other descriptive studies would be evaluated by a purpose-built AI reviewer, trained to assess methodological rigor in such studies and designed not to retain or learn from unpublished manuscripts. Accepted papers would appear in a companion journal or section of the parent title. Traditional peer review would then be reserved for longitudinal, experimental, and other higher-impact research. Beyond easing reviewer burden, this model creates a transparent signal of rigor that could help tenure and promotion committees reward quality over publication quantity.
evidence_items.title: Rethinking Peer Review in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Tiered Model for Health Promotion Journals.

evidence_items.summary: Plant-derived preparations remain widely used, yet their clinical application is constrained by multicomponent composition, batch-to-batch chemical variability, and complex pharmacokinetics, poorly characterized interactions, and marked interindividual variability in response. Artificial intelligence (AI) and computational pharmacology offer analytical tools suited to the high-dimensional data generated by phytomedicine, but enthusiasm has outpaced the supporting evidence. This critical narrative review evaluates AI applications across the phytomedicine pipeline, grading them by the strength and directness of evidence from computational prediction through in vitro, animal, observational, and randomized clinical studies. We organize the field around a Patient-Product-Mechanism-Response (PPMR) framework, arguing that meaningful personalization requires joint characterization of both the patient and the chemically variable botanical product. Current applications are most mature for botanical authentication, spectral annotation, quality assurance, and mechanism-informed hypothesis generation, whereas validated tools for patient stratification, individualized product and dose selection, and improved clinical outcomes remain limited. Rather than claiming efficacy gains, we present AI as a means to advance standardized, mechanism-informed, and testable phytomedicine, contingent on higher-quality data, prospective external validation, and regulatory alignment. The central finding is that none of the studies examined demonstrated a complete AI-guided personalized-phytomedicine pathway from joint patient-and-product characterization through a prospectively validated individualized response; precision phytomedicine should therefore be described as an emerging and hypothesis-generating research programme rather than an established clinical capability.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Precision Phytomedicine: A Critical Review and the Patient-Product-Mechanism-Response (PPMR) Framework.

evidence_items.summary: This paper introduces a framework for the packaging of components in a vehicle's threedimensional structure that is grounded in evidence and reproducible when taking advantage of the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The public OSU–Honda CarHoods10k dataset provides over 10,000 3D hood-frame designs based on 109 parameterized designs, along with design parameters and finite element (FE) performance data. The data package is about 45.66 GB, including design parameters and finite-element (FE) performance data. This dataset is not a multi-component vehicle-layout dataset and can't be used for a complete validation of a vehicle packaging optimizer: thermal, service access, or assembly data of the vehicle are not available at the component level. The studies of published adjacent work have shown that an improved solution with 3 times less computational budget could be offered, a result specific to this study but not predicted for automotive packaging. The proposed framework formalizes the placement variables, geometric constraints, engineering constraints, a model of screening by an artificial neural network (ANN), and a genetic search by NSGA- II, where the two objectives change. It also defines a controlled validation protocol to manual and rule-based baselines. There are no new vehicle-program performance gains since no proprietary vehicle-program layout dataset, executable code, or experimental logs for auditing were provided. The applicable vehicle-program specifications and relevant standards should supply acceptance limits.
evidence_items.title: AI Integration in Automotive Packaging Engineering for Multi-Constraint Component Optimization

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Clinical documentation is a cornerstone of safe, high-quality healthcare, yet has become an increasingly burdensome task for clinicians. Artificial Intelligence (AI) scribes have emerged as a promising solution to this problem, ambiently capturing clinical encounters and alleviating administrative load. Rapid deployment has occurred across healthcare settings, with many commercial options entering the market. However, adoption has outpaced development of rigorous evaluation frameworks, with no existing standardised method of evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical documentation across products.


OBJECTIVE
To review the existing literature on AI scribe implementation and clinical documentation quality evaluation, identify limitations of current approaches, and establish the conceptual foundations and domain requirements for a purpose-built evaluation instrument.


METHODS
A narrative review was conducted, searching MEDLINE, Embase and Google Scholar in March 2026 with supplementary reference list screening. Records were screened by title, abstract and full text for relevance to AI scribe outcomes and error patterns, clinical documentation functions, and note quality instruments. Approximately 60 records were identified, and 41 references are cited, including background references and publications added during the revision.


RESULTS
AI scribes consistently demonstrate reduced documentation burden and improved clinician wellbeing, however there are limited existing evaluative frameworks.Six recurring functions of clinical documentation were identified, and four AI-associated error patterns emerged: hallucination, misattribution, omissions and intent distortion. Instruments designed for human-authored documentation may be insensitive to these. AI-targeted adaptations incompletely address these gaps. Equity and linguistic bias remain largely unaddressed, with stigmatising language present in AI drafts and incompletely removed at clinician sign-off.


CONCLUSIONS
There is a clear need for a validated, theoretically grounded evaluation framework designed specifically for AI-generated clinical documentation. Such an instrument should assess fidelity and attribution, faithfulness to clinician intent, transmission of clinical reasoning, downstream interpretability, and decision accountability, whilst assessing equity and context as cross-cutting considerations.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating AI-generated clinical documentation: a narrative review of quality frameworks and the case for a purpose-built instrument.

evidence_items.summary: Given their real-time responsive capabilities, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have been positioned as cognitive partners for young children. However, research and policy directives have tended toward technological determinism, which black-boxes how these technologies function in early childhood education (ECE). Applying Actor-Network Theory (ANT), this qualitative case study deconstructs pedagogical black boxes during a plant inquiry unit involving a teacher, four children (aged 5–6), and AI-integrated devices. The findings provide a typology of three pedagogical black boxes: operational (obscuring technical constraints), epistemic (obscuring knowledge construction), and relational (obscuring negotiations of agency and classroom authority). Analysis of the case illustrated how these black boxes opened through distance (children’s communication gaps), breakdown (AI errors), and innovation (negotiation over AI use), revealing hidden dynamics in AI integration, such as uncertainty, people at work, decisions, competition, and controversies. Teacher scaffolding emerged as a key mediator of child-AI interactions, translating children’s open-ended inquiries into AI-legible inputs, transforming AI errors into opportunities for evaluative judgement, and recalibrating children’s AI interactions into child-led scientific inquiry. Ultimately, the paper shows that the seamless integration of AI is neither realistic nor pedagogically effective, and exemplifies how emergent frictions can foster young learners’ AI literacy, evaluative judgement, and relational agency.
evidence_items.title: Scaffolding young children’s AI use: opening pedagogical black boxes in early childhood classrooms

evidence_items.summary: Harm-benefit analysis (HBA) is one pillar of Directive 2010/63/EU, which regulates the use of animals in biomedical research. Despite HBA's central role in legislation governing in vivo studies, its regulatory adequacy is often questioned. In particular, it is widely acknowledged that the proper implementation of HBA is hampered by the vagueness of current policies, especially those related to assessing benefit. This review examined how benefit is interpreted in HBA, reconstructing the most prominent views emerging from the current debate and their implications for scientific practice. It reviews recent literature on this topic to identify the main issues arising from the ambiguity of the benefit concept and then reflects on their impact on the regulatory process for animal research. The artificial intelligence tool ChatPDF was used to facilitate the analysis of the sources. The findings suggest three central considerations: (1) scarce value is attributed to the epistemic benefits of preclinical trials, (2) the ethical evaluation of in vivo project proposals should better account for experimental quality and validity, and (3) it is essential to bridge the growing gap between the scientific community and society by promoting public understanding and engagement with biomedicine to rebuild trust in research.
evidence_items.title: Cui Bono? Characterisation of the benefit concept and the justificatory narratives in animal research ethics literature.

evidence_items.summary:
OBJECTIVE
Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve prostate MRI interpretation and reduce radiologist workload, but evidence supporting clinical implementation remains limited. This scoping review summarises evidence on commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI.


MATERIALS AND METHODS
PubMed was searched for studies published through October 1, 2026. Eligible devices were cleared by the United States Food and Drug Administration and/or CE marked, with commercial availability corroborated through manufacturer websites. Data extraction addressed standalone AI performance, AI-assisted radiologist performance, workflow efficiency, and downstream clinical impact.


RESULTS
Twenty-one studies evaluating 7 commercial AI systems were included; 17/21 (81%) were retrospective and 14/21 (67%) were single-centre. AI assistance suggested greater benefit for less-experienced readers, but improvements were inconsistent and increased specificity sometimes accompanied reduced sensitivity. Standalone evaluations, outside the devices' approved intended use, showed discrimination comparable to that of radiologists in selected cohorts. Inter-reader agreement and workflow benefits were mixed. We identify three key limitations of the current body of evidence that require thoughtful consideration before routine implementation: (1) incomplete verification strategies, (2) limited determination of workflow benefit, and (3) lack of analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes, e.g., time to treat or cancer-free survival.


CONCLUSION
Evidence supporting the use of commercial AI for prostate MRI remains limited and heterogeneous, with inconsistent diagnostic benefits. Prospective comparative studies in real clinical workflows are needed to determine its potential role within the prostate cancer diagnostic pathway.


KEY POINTS
Question Evidence for clinical implementation of prostate AI remains limited-most studies are retrospective and single-centre, with heterogeneous populations and reference standards. Findings AI may improve diagnostic performance for less-experienced readers, but gains for expert readers and assessment of workflow efficiency are limited. Clinical relevance Prospective multicentre studies embedded in real-world pathways are needed, together with analyses of cost-effectiveness and patient outcomes.
evidence_items.title: Commercially available AI medical devices for prostate MRI: current evidence and opportunities for implementation.

evidence_items.summary: KEY POINTS Question: How has billed use of artificial intelligence (AI)-related CPT codes changed nationally since 2021, and how does use differ by patient, geographic, and payer characteristics? Findings: In this cross-sectional study of 11.6 billion US encounters, 2.9 per 100,000 included an AI-required CPT code. Odds of use were nearly 10 times higher in 2025 than in 2021, higher among Medicare beneficiaries, and lower among Medicaid enrollees and residents of socially vulnerable areas. Meaning: Billed AI use remains rare and uneven across payers and communities, so payment policy for AI may need to be paired with monitoring of who receives AI-enabled care. ABSTRACT Importance: Payment policy for clinical artificial intelligence (AI) is changing quickly, yet national data on which AI-enabled services are used, and for whom, are limited. Objective: To describe national trends in the use of AI-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes and how use differs by patient, geographic, and payer characteristics. Design, Setting, and Participants: This serial cross-sectional study used Epic Cosmos, a deidentified electronic health record dataset, to examine 11,605,867,309 encounters among 233,628,292 US patients from January 1, 2021, to April 14, 2026. Exposures: Calendar year, age, sex, race, ethnicity, rurality, area-level social vulnerability, census region, and primary payer. Main Outcomes and Measures: Encounters with any of 65 CPT codes that require AI, identified by matching the CPT code set to US Food and Drug Administration-listed AI-enabled devices and classified as assistive, augmentative, or autonomous using the CPT Appendix S taxonomy. Results: Of 11.6 billion encounters, 335,349 (2.9 per 100,000) included an AI-required CPT code. The odds of an encounter with an AI-required code were 9.88 (95% CI, 9.71-10.06) times higher in 2025 than in 2021. In unadjusted comparisons, use was higher among patients aged 65 to 85 years and among those with Medicare (OR, 5.11) or Medicare Advantage (OR, 5.12) vs commercial insurance. Use was lower among Black (OR, 0.72) and Hispanic or Latino (OR, 0.34) patients, Medicaid enrollees (OR, 0.65), residents of the most socially vulnerable areas (OR, 0.53), and residents of the most rural areas (OR, 0.86). Use of automated diabetic retinopathy screening increased after the service was added to a HEDIS quality measure. One newer code (quantitative brain MRI) appeared in rural areas within months of becoming effective, whereas older codes such as retinopathy screening took years. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cross-sectional study, billed use of AI-enabled services remained rare but grew substantially and was concentrated among older and Medicare-insured patients, with lower use among Medicaid enrollees and residents of socially vulnerable areas. As the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services restructures payment for software and launches outcome-based models, tracking who receives AI-enabled care across payment pathways will be important for equitable access.
evidence_items.title: Use of AI-Related CPT Codes by Patient, Geographic, and Payer Characteristics in the U.S., 2021-2026

evidence_items.summary: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the automobile banking industry and its impact on the business processes is very fast, the impact of AI techniques in financial performance is not fully understood. The challenge here is that banks involved in the automotive sector often have fragmented disclosures of AI and inconsistent metrics, making it challenging to come up with accurate predictions of the financial impact of AI. To address this gap, they propose a model known as “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries. To fill this gap, they propose a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.in the automobile banking industry has transformed business processes, yet how AI techniques influence financial performance is not yet fully understood. The difficulty here lies in scattered AI disclosures and disparate metrics that hinder effective forecasts of financial results in car-related banks. In order to bridge this gap, the research introduces a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.” The analysis relies on a dataset called “AI Techniques on Financial Performance of Automobile Industries,” which contains 131 annual report records for sixteen Indian-listed banks from 2015 to 2023. This dataset captures keyword-based AI disclosures, as well as institutional and financial indicators. Data pre-processing is done through the use of the Correlation Coefficient with Min–Max Weighted (CCMMW) method to normalize and fine-tune the input parameters, while the Masked Attention Mask Transformer (Mask2Former) is utilized for feature extraction for isolating the disclosure patterns that have the greatest influence. Following these steps, a Self-Guided Quantum Generative Adversarial Network (SG-QGAN) is constructed and then advanced into the new Residual Self-Guided Quantum Single-Head Generative Elk Herd Vision Adversarial Attention Network (RSG-QSAGE-HV2AN). This network combines SG-QGAN with a Residual Attention Single-Head Vision Transformer Network (RA-SHViT-Net) and fine-tunes its parameters with the Elk Herd Optimizer (EHO). This work aims to propose a new hybrid approach named RSG-QSAGE-HV2AN to forecast AI derived financial performance of automobile financing banks. The data set is composed of ` (2015–2023), which is divided into 80% training and 20% testing. The 5-fold cross validation is used to guarantee robustness. The accuracy of the proposed model is 99.98% (95% confidence interval [99.98 ± 0.72%]) which is much better than the conventional model (Random Forest and XGBoost). The framework is combined with CCMMW pre-processing, feature extraction using Mask2Former, SG-QGAN with EHO optimized RA-SHViT-net. The results of experiments show the higher predictive performance, interpretability (through the use of SHAP) and lower computation cost.
evidence_items.title: Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries

evidence_items.summary: Nanomaterials have significantly advanced biosensor development by enabling highly efficient sensing interfaces with enhanced sensitivity, selectivity, signal amplification, and analytical performance. This narrative review provides a comprehensive overview of the main classes of nanomaterials used in biosensing, including metallic nanoparticles, carbon-based nanomaterials, quantum dots, and hybrid nanocomposites. This review focuses on the physicochemical mechanisms by which these materials improve biosensor performance, including increased electroactive surface area, accelerated electron transfer, electrocatalytic activity, optical signal enhancement, and stable biofunctionalization of recognition elements. This review discusses key immobilization strategies in relation to their effects on sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, and operational stability. Representative biosensor platforms are critically evaluated according to their detection mechanisms, analytical performance, advantages, limitations, and applications in clinical diagnostics, environmental monitoring, food safety, and pharmaceutical analysis. Hybrid nanomaterials emerge as particularly promising because they combine complementary properties within a single sensing interface, enabling improved electron transfer, greater active surface area, enhanced bioreceptor immobilization, reduced overpotentials, and amplified analytical signals. Despite substantial progress, important challenges remain regarding reproducibility, long-term stability, biocompatibility, selectivity in complex matrices, standardized fabrication, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory validation. Future research should therefore prioritize translating high-performance laboratory prototypes into robust, scalable analytical platforms validated on complex real samples. Integrating nanomaterials with screen-printed electrodes, paper-based devices, wearable sensors, microfluidics, smartphone-assisted platforms, and artificial intelligence is expected to drive the next generation of biosensing technologies. These advances may enable more accessible, portable, cost-effective, and reliable biosensors for point-of-care diagnostics, personalized healthcare, environmental monitoring, food safety, and pharmaceutical analysis.
evidence_items.title: Nanomaterials applied in biosensor development

evidence_items.summary: Porous magneto-electro-elastic (PMEE) nanoshells offer lightweight, field-tunable structural concepts for nano-electromechanical systems, but their post-buckling response is governed simultaneously by porosity, small-scale mechanics, geometric nonlinearity, and multi-field coupling. This study develops a nonlinear model based on the nonlocal strain gradient theory (NSGT) for functionally graded PMEE cylindrical nanoshells using Kirchhoff-Love kinematics, von Kármán nonlinearity, coupled magneto-electro-elastic constitutive relations, and Galerkin continuation. Symmetric/asymmetric cosine porosity distributions and distinct symmetric/asymmetric buckling branches are considered. Modal convergence and two quantitative benchmark families in the local homogeneous elastic limit support the numerical implementation; the maximum discrepancies from published critical-load data are 0.00752% and 0.02450%. At wmax/h = 0.38, increasing the porosity coefficient from 0 to 0.4 reduces the normalized load by 19.3–22.4%. Increasing e0a/h from 0 to 0.4 lowers the load by 0.83–2.16%, whereas increasing lm/h over the same range raises it by 1.63–2.22%, clearly separating nonlocal softening from strain-gradient hardening. Electric and magnetic potentials provide systematic but sub-1% tuning over the studied ranges. Increasing L/h reduces the critical load by 0.51–6.34% and can induce post-buckling branch crossings. The results identify porosity as the dominant load-level parameter, with size effects, fields, and geometry providing mode-dependent secondary control.
evidence_items.title: Post-buckling behavior of porous magneto-electro-elastic nano-cylindrical shells based on nonlocal strain gradient theory

evidence_items.summary: To the Editor Despite signi ﬁ cant therapeutic advances, most patients with multiple myeloma (MM) eventually relapse and require successive lines of therapy, with progressively shorter remissions and increasing drug refractoriness [1, 2]. Treatment patterns and outcomes of relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) patients in Asia differ substantially from those reported in Western populations due to differences in drug availability, reimbursement, healthcare infrastructure, access to clinical trials, patient and carer preferences [3], and potentially disease biology [4]. Despite these important differences, real-world data describing treatment sequencing and outcomes across Asia remain limited. We therefore conducted a multinational and multiregional Asian Myeloma Network (AMN) study to characterize real-world treatment patterns and clinical outcomes in MM patients receiving second line (2 L), third line (3 L), and fourth line (4 L) therapy, to provide a benchmark for RRMM treatment management across Asia. We performed a multicenter retrospective observational chart review study across six Asian countries and regions, including 1123 patients across 2 L ( N = 626), 3 L ( N = 341) and 4 L ( N = 156), treated between 2020 and 2022 (Supplementary Fig. 1). The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), while secondary endpoints included overall response rates (ORR), time to next treatment or death (TTNT), overall survival (OS) and prognostic factors associated with outcome. Eligibility criteria, response de ﬁ nitions, and statistical methods are provided in the Supplementary Methods. Baseline patient characteristics for the combined cohort and individual countries and regions are presented in Suppl. Tables 1 – 4. The median ages were 64, 63, and 61 years in the 2 L, 3 L, and
evidence_items.title: Real-world treatment patterns and clinical outcomes in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma across Asia: a multicenter Asian Myeloma Network study (AMN010)

evidence_items.summary: Chitosan and alginate offer complementary amino, hydroxyl and carboxylate functionality for the removal of dissolved metal contaminants. Their practical performance depends on chemical modification, network stability, solution composition and sorbent architecture. This narrative review examines modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration, with particular attention to chitosan-alginate hybrids. The review links polymer chemistry and fabrication to reported adsorption performance, distinguishing literature-reported capacities from evidence of mechanism and operational durability. A descriptive compilation identifies study-specific results and gaps in experimental reporting. It is not a normalised benchmark or a systematic meta-analysis. Hybridisation and functionalisation can improve selected properties, but the available cross-study data do not establish universal superiority over single-polymer sorbents or isolate donor chemistry from composition and test conditions. Langmuir and pseudo-second-order fits describe equilibrium and kinetic data without independently proving chemisorption or rate control. Within-study controls, explicit aqueous speciation, distinct desorption and capacity-retention metrics, and validation under competitive continuous-flow conditions are needed for defensible comparison and scale-up.
evidence_items.title: Chitosan- and alginate-based biopolymeric composites for the adsorption of heavy metal ions from wastewater: modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration.

evidence_items.summary: Fish-derived spheroid cultures offer a promising in vitro alternative to conventional cell culture by providing enhanced cell-cell interactions, and tissue-like metabolic heterogeneity. Although three-dimensional (3D) culture methods remain largely unexplored in fish cell systems, these features may provide a fit-for-purpose model for applications requiring prolonged culture periods, such as chronic toxicity. Here, we established and evaluated a 3D spheroid model using the RTgill-W1 cell line and compared its toxicological responses to conventional two-dimensional (2D) cultures. A proof-of-concept assessment was conducted using two well-known model metal-based ecotoxicants, CuSO₄ and K₂CrO₄, both found in heavy metal contaminations in water bodies due to their ubiquitous use in agriculture and industry. Uniform RTgill-W1 spheroids with diameters around 350 µm were reproducibly generated using agarose-coated round-bottom plates, enhanced by centrifugation and methylcellulose as extracellular matrix. Comparison of 2D and 3D cultures revealed that CuSO₄ responses were similar in both formats, whereas K₂CrO₄ toxicity was markedly reduced in spheroids, likely reflecting limited compound penetration. 3D culture results for K₂CrO₄ showed strong agreement with reported in vivo data, whereas CuSO₄ toxicity was underestimated, potentially due to its complexation with serum proteins. The distinct differences in toxicological outcomes and morphological alterations between 2D and 3D models suggest that spheroid cultures potentially provide a complementary platform with altered cellular interactions and response dynamics compared with conventional monolayer cultures. Our findings demonstrate that RTgill-W1 spheroids represent a robust and reproducible model for environmental toxicity testing, aligning with the principles of the 3Rs and advancing fish-based in vitro methodologies.
evidence_items.title: Fish gill spheroids as an advanced 3D in vitro system for ecotoxicological risk assessment.

evidence_items.summary: Through a combined approach, that involved the one-strain-many-compounds (OSMAC) culturing approach, metabolomic and genomic studies, and bioassay-guided purification we disclose the marine fungus Clonostachys rosea as producer of a family of peptaibols with new structural features. HRMS/MS, NMR, and advanced Marfey’s analysis enabled the structural elucidation of two major compounds of the roseabol family, named roseabols B (1) and C (2). Molecular networking further revealed a highly diverse and microheterogeneous peptaibol profile. Biological evaluation highlighted the ability of the isolated peptaibols to inhibit biofilm formation against Escherichia coli and Candida albicans. Overall, these studies demonstrate the effectiveness of metabolomics-driven strategies in discovering novel natural products and identify marine-derived peptaibols as promising antibiofilm agents.
evidence_items.title: Uncovering new antibiofilm roseabols from marine Clonostachys rosea through structural and multiomics approaches

evidence_items.summary: Orthopedic implants can become infected in hospitals requiring additional surgeries and device replacement. The pathogenesis of these device-associated bone infections is fundamentally driven by the transition of opportunistic pathogens from a free-floating planktonic state to a surface-bound, highly resilient biofilm state. Biofilms shield resident bacteria within a self-secreted extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix, making them up to 1000-fold more resistant to conventional systemic antibiotics and host-immune clearance. To overcome the clinical challenges of biofilm elimination, the field of regenerative bone biointerfaces is transitioning from traditional antibiotic therapies toward multifunctional, fully resorbable, dual-therapy biomaterial platforms. These modern architectures are engineered to simultaneously clear localized infections and orchestrate host bone tissue reconstruction within a single surgical window. This review provides a comprehensive categorization and critical evaluation of six breakthrough therapeutic themes shaping next-generation orthopedic scaffolds: (1) spatiotemporally optimized dual or multiple antibiotic delivery networks; (2) integrated antibiotic-osteogenic growth factor/peptide frameworks; (3) mechanistically direct biofilm matrix-disrupting enzyme matrices; (4) localized hyperthermic near-infrared (NIR) photothermal therapy combined with osteogenic scaffolds; (5) intrinsic antibiotic-free antimicrobial metal ion/nanoparticle scaffolds; and (6) alternative biological agent architectures leveraging bacteriophages or probiotic biofilms. This review summarizes the advantages, limitations, clinical potential, and future research directions of each therapeutic platform.
evidence_items.title: Dual-Therapy Resorbable Biomaterials to Eliminate Bone Infections and Biofilms.

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
This phase III, multicenter, randomized, open-label study (NCT05754333) evaluated pudexacianinium chloride (ASP5354), a novel near-infrared fluorescence (NIR-F) imaging agent, for intraoperative ureter identification in minimally invasive and open abdominopelvic surgeries.


METHODS
Patients with normal renal function, mild renal impairment, or patients with moderately impaired renal function received one intravenous dose of pudexacianinium 3 mg intraoperatively. Investigators scored ureter conspicuity under white light (WL) or (WL+)NIR-F using a validated 5-point Likert scale. Primary and key secondary endpoints included intra-participant differences in conspicuity scores for WL versus (WL+)NIR-F, supported by blinded central image review and quantitative contrast enhancement factor (CEF) analysis.


RESULTS
Adults with normal renal function or mild renal impairment were randomly assigned in a 5:1 ratio to WL+NIR-F arm (intent-to-treat population, n = 72 [median age 55.0 years; 68.1% female]) or to WL-only arm (n = 13 [median age 64.0 years; 76.9% female]). Eight adults with moderate renal impairment (median age 70.0 years; 75.0% female) and 14 adolescents with normal renal function or mild renal impairment (median age 14.5 years; 57.1% female) were imaged under WL+NIR-F (no randomization). In the same participants of intent-to-treat population, (WL+)NIR-F yielded significantly higher conspicuity scores than WL, both 30 min (± 15) postdose and at end of surgery, confirmed by central review and CEF analysis. Benefits persisted to 210 min post-injection (timepoints with ≥ 5 evaluable patients). No drug-related serious adverse events occurred, and most treatment-emergent adverse events were mild- or moderate-grade. Adults with moderate renal impairment had higher mean plasma pudexacianinium concentrations and slower urinary excretion than adults with normal renal function or mild renal impairment. Adolescents had numerically lower mean urine production rates and higher mean urine pudexacianinium concentrations than adults.


CONCLUSIONS
Pudexacianinium is an effective visualization agent without invasive instrumentation. NIR-F imaging with pudexacianinium enhances ureter identification compared with WL-only, which may reduce risk of intraoperative ureter injury.
evidence_items.title: Pudexacianinium chloride (ASP5354) for ureter visualization in patients undergoing abdominopelvic surgery: a phase III, multicenter, open-label, randomized study.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Mpox has shifted from a disease mainly associated with zoonotic spillover in Central and West Africa to a recurrent global public-health threat involving sexual-contact networks, household transmission, international mobility, ecological persistence and clade-specific uncertainty. Mathematical models have clarified important mechanisms in the 2022 clade IIb outbreak, including the role of heavy-tailed sexual-contact distributions, behavioural adaptation, vaccination and case isolation. However, the literature remains less mature in one respect that is essential for preparedness: the conversion of transmission insight into reliable, setting-specific forecasts. This narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed modelling evidence on mpox transmission patterns and evaluates the extent to which existing compartmental, stochastic, network, agent-based, phylodynamic and time-series models support future outbreak prediction. The review identifies four recurring gaps: insufficient prospective validation, weak integration of spatial and cross-regional lags, limited clade-specific parameterization for clade I/Ib risk, and inadequate incorporation of immunity, reporting delay and surveillance uncertainty. We propose a forecasting-oriented framework that links epidemiological state variables, contact structure, population immunity, mobility, interventions and uncertainty quantification to decision-relevant outputs. The novelty of this review lies in repositioning mpox modelling from retrospective explanation toward predictive readiness. A forecasting-first approach can strengthen early warning, targeted vaccination, communication planning and health-system preparedness, particularly in settings where surveillance is delayed, incomplete or geographically fragmented.
evidence_items.title: Transmission patterns and future forecasting of mpox: a review of mathematical modelling approaches for prediction and public health preparedness

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND
Evidence for multi-agent intradiscal and epidural injection in suspected discogenic low back pain is limited. We evaluated a mixture of botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A), lidocaine, triamcinolone, and dextrose.


METHODS
Adults undergoing the combined procedure were reviewed retrospectively. Under fluoroscopy, a transforaminal approach through Kambin's triangle permitted intradiscal injection followed by needle withdrawal for contrast-confirmed ventral epidural injection through the same corridor. Visual analog scale (VAS) scores were assessed at baseline, one week, one month, and three months. Paired comparisons accounted for repeated procedures within patients. Responder thresholds were reductions of at least 2 points, 30%, or 50%. Missing three-month outcomes were classified as nonresponse in a sensitivity analysis.


RESULTS
The analysis comprised 113 procedures in 88 patients. Follow-up VAS was available for 106, 87, and 73 procedures. Mean VAS decreased from 7.9 to 3.7, 3.8, and 4.3; the three-month paired reduction was 3.6 points (95% CI, 2.7-4.5; P < 0.001). At three months, 45/73 procedures (62%) achieved at least 30% improvement; the missing-as-nonresponse estimate was 45/113 (40%). Among 34 procedures with an early score before loss to three-month follow-up, 22 (65%) had at least 30% improvement. Two adverse events occurred among 115 safety-reviewed procedures (1.7%): transient bilateral leg weakness requiring hospitalization and self-limited dysgeusia.


CONCLUSIONS
This four-agent, dual-site protocol showed a preliminary short-term pain-response signal. The uncontrolled design cannot isolate a BoNT-A effect or confirm the proposed neural mechanisms. Prospective controlled evaluation and safety monitoring are required.
evidence_items.title: Fluoroscopy-Guided Combined Intradiscal and Transforaminal Ventral Epidural Injection Containing Botulinum Toxin Type A and Steroid for Suspected Discogenic Low Back Pain: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

evidence_items.summary: Plant-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using agricultural by-products is not only a strategy to develop sustainable nanoparticle synthesis methods but also helps address environmental pollution caused by agricultural waste. In this study, Siamese banana peel (SBP) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of AgNPs. The effects of reaction time, AgNO3 solution concentration, and the volume ratio between the AgNO3 solution and banana peel extract on the formation of AgNPs were evaluated using UV-Vis spectroscopy via surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The physicochemical characteristics of AgNPs under optimal conditions were assessed via UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and HR-TEM analyses. Antibacterial activity was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) against nine microbial strains, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. The results showed that the suitable synthesis conditions included a reaction time of 120 minutes, an AgNO3 concentration of 2.0 mM, and an AgNO3 solution-to-extract volume ratio of 30 : 20 (v/v). Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis revealed that the nanoparticles were predominantly spherical, well-dispersed, with sizes ranging within 28.3 ± 10.1 nm. XRD and selected area electron diffraction (SAED) analyses indicated that the AgNPs possessed a face-centered cubic (fcc) crystalline structure of metallic silver, whereas FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of phytochemical functional groups involved in nanoparticle formation and surface stabilization. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited antibacterial activity across all tested strains, with MIC/MBC ratios ranging from 2 to 4, demonstrating significant bactericidal efficacy under the experimental conditions.
evidence_items.title: Siamese banana peel-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles and their broad-spectrum antibacterial activity.

evidence_items.summary:
PURPOSE
NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with radiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitors pyrimethamine and its potent analog, WCDD115, as radiosensitizing agents through disruption of one-carbon metabolism.


PATIENTS AND METHODS
Preclinical studies used NRF2-competent and deficient HNSCC models, clonogenic assays, transcriptomics, metabolomics, pharmacokinetics/toxicity testing, and syngeneic tumor grafts to assess WCDD115 as a novel radiosensitizing agent. In parallel, we conducted an open-label, single-center, window-of-opportunity early phase I clinical trial (NCT05678348) of previously untreated patients with HPV(-) stage III/IV HNSCC to receive pyrimethamine 50mg prior to surgery. Correlative analysis included mass spectrometry, western blotting, and pathway analysis.


RESULTS
WCDD115 enhanced radiation-induced DNA damage and suppressed one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide biosynthesis. Parallel mouse tumor studies demonstrated that WCDD115 enhanced the efficacy of radiation in NRF2-competent but not NRF2-deficient tumors. In a clinical trial of neoadjuvant pyrimethamine, DHFR protein expression was enriched post-treatment by a mean fold change of 9.91 (95% confidence interval 8.1 to 12.2), consistent with a strong on-target effect. The drug was well tolerated with no drug-related grade 3-5 adverse events or surgical delays.


CONCLUSIONS
NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with enhanced one-carbon metabolism which can be therapeutically targeted with DHFR inhibitors to promote radiation sensitization. In HNSCC patients, pyrimethamine achieves potent DHFR inhibition and a favorable safety profile supporting a future phase 2 trial integrating pyrimethamine with definitive radiation-based therapy for NRF2-active HNSCCs.
evidence_items.title: Targeting DHFR to suppress one-carbon metabolism and enhance radiation sensitivity in patients with NRF2-active head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

evidence_items.summary:
INTRODUCTION
Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance.


METHODS
We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples.


RESULTS
We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains.


CONCLUSION
This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.
evidence_items.title: Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro and chikungunya viruses as causative agents of febrile syndrome in Colombian patients during 2013 and 2014.

evidence_items.summary: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality. The second key addresses a modality misalignment between context prefilling and novel-view rendering: we disentangle context tokens into camera-only context rendering tokens to serve as TTB input, and context ground-truth tokens with image content to serve as the TTB mapping target, ensuring the baked MLPs are relieved of the modality generalization challenge between context and novel-view processing. Our method achieves up to **23x** rendering speedup with quality on par with the state-of-the-art across several benchmarks. Project page: https://test-time-baking.github.io
evidence_items.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models

evidence_items.summary: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require. We find that decision information is concentrated in intermediate layers, with early layers building essential features and the final six layers removable without loss, while independently trained smaller models largely mimic the full model rather than developing specialized decision capabilities. These findings suggest that efficiency requires not simply smaller backbones, but shared computation across different depths. Building on this, we propose , which jointly trains a full model with prefix sub-models that share its final layers and decision head through self-distillation. A lightweight gate reads the hidden state at each exit to determine whether additional computation is needed, allowing one model to operate at multiple layers. Across seven decision benchmarks, our approach matches or outperforms independently trained models at every depth, while achieving better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs through adaptive computation.
evidence_items.title: From Large Language Models to Efficient System One Models via Adaptive Computation

evidence_items.summary: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along ceilings on rollout count and feedback fidelity. Comparing self-evolving with fixed loops within each scenario separates the limitations that the scenario imposes from those inherent in the self-evolving design. We then recast each mechanism as a trade-off that raises a scarce factor by presupposing a task-structural resource, such as output equivalence or checkable outcomes, and judge it portable, conditional, blocked, or redundant across scenarios. We attribute the asymmetry to divergent combinations of scarce factors and resources across opposite transfer directions, and identify the matched-budget measurements that could overturn these still untested verdicts.
evidence_items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents

evidence_items.summary: Adversarial training is often plagued by "pseudo-attacks", perturbations that significantly increase the loss value but fail to truly alter the model's confidence structure. To address this, we propose two complementary approaches to directly attack and defend against confidence structure deformation. First, building upon the traditional loss maximization perspective, we introduce a hybrid objective that integrates cross-entropy and KL divergence, encouraging adversarial examples to simultaneously disrupt prediction accuracy and distribution consistency. Second, we geometrically reconstruct adversarial training by generating perturbations that maximize the distribution distance on the confidence manifold. Theoretical analysis shows that the optimal perturbation direction aligns with the principal eigenvectors of the Fisher information matrix. We also propose an efficient algorithm to avoid high-dimensional matrix computations. Experiments on multiple datasets and model architectures demonstrate that our method outperforms existing methods in adversarial robustness and robust transferability, particularly excelling in structural perturbations within high-confidence regions.
evidence_items.title: Structured Confidence Perturbation via Fisher Geometry for Adversarial Training

evidence_items.summary: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the predicted future. The BEV, rendered from scene annotations for training, depicts roads and vehicles as simple shapes at a fixed metric scale, providing a top-down view of their positions and motion with reduced occlusion between vehicles. Perspective video, by contrast, retains scene details that the BEV omits, such as traffic signals and object appearance. Joint attention between two video diffusion transformers, one per stream, lets each stream inform the other during generation. The predicted BEV also provides a geometric interface for ego control: we translate and rotate its latest frame along an input ego trajectory and use the resulting frames as a soft condition that shows how the scene would appear to move if only the ego vehicle moved. At inference, BirdDreams generates both videos from a single camera image without requiring an HD map or vehicle-state inputs. On PhysicalAI-AV and nuScenes, BirdDreams follows input ego trajectories more faithfully than prior driving world models and generates more plausible ego motion without ego-action conditioning. Human evaluation shows that BirdDreams outperforms a perspective-only baseline in generating realistic surrounding-vehicle behavior.
evidence_items.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model

evidence_items.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \hivemem, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textsc{H}or\textsc{i}zontal Memory Expansion with \textsc{Ve}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.
evidence_items.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents

evidence_items.summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution, our model delivers a \(20\times\) speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.
evidence_items.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation

evidence_items.summary: Tool timeouts can leave AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes and partial execution: an action may have failed, committed or remained in flight while other workflow steps have already completed. We formulate evidence-guided task recovery over approved obligations, provider capabilities and states compatible with public evidence. A shared admissibility check handles key expiry, authorization timing, dependencies and residual effects; a terminal certificate separates actual goal satisfaction from publicly supported safe completion. The known-model implementation combines standard observation-contingent planning with a separately implemented effect-history adjudicator. In a finite study of 37 assignments, planning and three active controls each certify 28 completions; four saved synthetic fee units incur additional computation. A preregistered assignment-held-out comparison then evaluates planning advice against evidence prompting with two local model bundles. Across 58 paired units in 19 previously developed task families, advice certifies 30 completions versus 9, a 36.2-percentage-point difference (exact family sign-flip p=0.0078), using 272 proposals versus 399. All 116 trajectories pass independent replay. Both models exhibit a positive completion difference. The comparison measures the evaluated advice interface under a common shield; search-versus-rule advice requires a separate matched comparison. Unknown and handoff outcomes remain explicit, with guarantees tied to the declared provider capabilities rather than arbitrary third-party exactly-once execution.
evidence_items.title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution

evidence_items.summary: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. Each spectrum is shown as four tables (nm, μm, scientific notation, eV) and two plots (nm, eV), and partial spectra remove data inside or outside the queried range. We evaluate the decision models d3-nano and Jev 1.13, three GPT-6 Luna configurations and the Qwen3.5-2B base model. Changing only the representation moves accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model, mostly on photon-energy tables and plots. With the same evidence, asking in photon energy instead of wavelength helps some model-view pairs by 16-50 points and hurts others by up to 25. When the relevant extremum is removed, unadapted models rarely answer "undetermined". LoRA fine-tuning of d3-nano improves comparisons on the trained table formats, but much of its gain on unanswerable questions comes from a shortcut: it abstains whenever the input is truncated. Training with answerable truncations avoids the shortcut in all six seeds, with a 90-100 point gap between abstention after inside and outside cuts on held-out structures; with the same amount of extra original-task data, five of six seeds keep the shortcut. On gold spectra the two training sets perform similarly. Multimodal language models used for scientific decisions should be tested on equivalent representations and on missing evidence, not only on average accuracy. We release the tasks, per-response results and analysis code.
evidence_items.title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?

evidence_items.summary: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive. We check whether numbers, dates, person and organization names, and quoted spans survive each rewrite, using a rule-based checker validated by two AI annotators (precision 0.84-1.00, recall 0.93-0.95; no human annotation). In the October 2026 cycle of a public humanizer leaderboard, all 11 commercial tools changed or dropped at least one of these units in 35-65% of the documents that contained one. Most changes were to quoted spans; counting numbers and names alone, 10 of the 11 tools still altered at least one in 20% or more of the documents. The September 2026 cycle was similar (19-50%). An open 12B humanizer kept at least 97% of numbers and names in fact-dense U.S. federal agency text, but reworded 67-78% of the quoted spans, against its own prompt. Unit retention and detector evasion were not clearly related across tools (Spearman rho = -0.46, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.08), and the open model's four released files (two of them quantization-aware low-bit files) did not show the pre-registered monotone trade-off. On federal texts with matched human, AI-styled and humanized versions, a general-purpose decision model, Jev, asked a single zero-shot question, separated human originals from humanized rewrites with AUROC 0.864 (0.827-0.902), 0.18-0.22 higher than Binoculars, Fast-DetectGPT and the adversarially trained RADAR, while calling 24% of the human originals AI at a 0.5 threshold. On the AI-styled rewrites by 2026 models, both perplexity-based detectors scored below chance (AUROC 0.37 and 0.39), also with line breaks removed. Hypotheses, data rules and analyses were frozen before the main runs; two earlier data contacts are disclosed. We release the checker and the per-item results.
evidence_items.title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
